I saw a headline about your game being late. Is that the whole story?
Not even half. They confirmed November, and then they refused to take any question about money.
So they hid behind the date. Did anybody there say sorry?
The director did. She apologized for the silence and admitted that the last six months had been hard.
That is more than I expected. And the account that got the story first?
She denied reading it. They threatened to sue him three weeks ago and then dropped it.
You are calmer about this than I would be. Are you still buying it?
A producer warned that November leaves no time for testing, and he recommends that everybody wait for the reviews. So I am waiting.

Hi Mark. Last class you spent an hour on the smallest words in English, a, the, and nothing at all. Today the words get bigger and the difficulty moves somewhere else. When you report what somebody said, you almost never repeat the words. You choose one verb that carries the attitude, and that single verb tells the listener whether the person was defending themselves, giving in, or attacking somebody. He said he had not seen it tells me nothing. He denied seeing it tells me he was under pressure. Here is the part that costs Brazilian students marks. Each of these verbs takes its own pattern, and the pattern is not a matter of taste. Refuse, promise and threaten take to plus the infinitive. The studio refused to comment. Admit, deny and suggest take the ing form. She admitted changing the ending. Urge, persuade, advise and warn take an object first and then to plus the infinitive. Fans urged the studio to delay it. Accuse takes of, and apologize takes for, and both of them are followed by the ing form. They accused the studio of hiding the delay. And then there is suggest, which is the one that catches almost everybody. You cannot say he suggested me to wait. In English you say he suggested that I wait, or he suggested waiting. There is no version with an object and to. Before class, find any interview in English and write down every reporting verb the writer chose instead of said. See you on Friday, Mark.

Good evening, and welcome to the entertainment desk. The main story tonight comes from a press conference that lasted forty minutes and answered almost nothing. The studio has confirmed that the sequel will now arrive in November, five months later than the date printed on the poster in every station in this city. The director admitted that the last half of the year had been hard on the team, and she apologized for the silence, which is more than most studios manage. She then insisted that nobody had been asked to work through weekends, and she refused to take a single question about money. A fan account that reported the delay three weeks before the studio did was not mentioned by name. That account had accused the studio of hiding a much bigger problem, and the studio threatened to take legal action, then dropped it a week later without explanation. Asked about it on Tuesday, the director denied reading the account at all, and suggested that whoever writes it should apply for a job. Two people who were in the room have urged the studio to delay it again rather than ship it half finished, and one producer, who asked us not to use his name, recommends that fans stop pre-ordering until the reviews are out. He warned that November leaves almost no time for testing. The studio has promised to show forty minutes of the game in September, and has advised players to trust the official channel and nothing else. That is the news.

First, open with the fact that is now official, because that is the only line most people will read. Then report what the person accepted, using admit, and keep the verb doing the work instead of a long explanation. After that, report what the person defended, using insist, so the reader can hear that there was pressure in the room. Next, report what the person would not do, using refuse, because silence is news too. Finally, close with what somebody else wants to happen, using urge or recommend, so the story ends looking forward rather than backwards.
